sources.title: Randy Hampton
sources.text: Randy Hampton Research Publications Biography Research Our group studies a variety of questions that surround how the cell selectively destroys proteins. This work started with understanding how these sorts of mechanisms are employed to allow regulation of cellular cholesterol synthesis. These studies are ongoing and have led us in a number of interesting directions including cellular management of misfolded proteins, lipid signaling, and the dynamics of the ER and other organelles. For a complete picture of what we’ve done, what we do, and what we want to do, see the Hampton lab web site listed above. Thanks for stopping by! Welcome to the Hampton lab webpage! We are located in the Biology department at the University of California, San Diego. Our research interests lie in the regulated degradation of HMGCoA-reductase (HMGR) and in ER protein degradation in general. Our model organism is Saccharomyces cerevisiae , or budding yeast. We have included here information about our research, publications, protocols, and lab members. We welcome your comments and questions.
